description: Due-diligence questions used to smoke-test the agent built in Session 2 (preparation.md §4.5). Not an evaluation dataset — Session 4 measures faithfulness on paragraph_claims.json instead. 'answerable' records whether the corpus in data/02_processed/ actually contains the answer; questions marked false are deliberate, to reveal whether the agent admits ignorance or invents an answer. Page numbers refer to the trimmed PDFs in data/02_processed/, not the originals in 01_raw/.

questions.question: What was NVIDIA's total revenue in fiscal year 2026?
questions.source: 10-K 2026, p. 48, Consolidated Statements of Income — $215,938 million

questions.question: How did NVIDIA's revenue change between fiscal year 2025 and fiscal year 2026?
questions.source: 10-K 2026, p. 48, Consolidated Statements of Income — $130,497M to $215,938M, about +65%. Also derivable by comparing the two filings.

questions.question: How much did NVIDIA spend on research and development in fiscal year 2026?
questions.source: 10-K 2026, p. 48, Consolidated Statements of Income — $18,497 million

questions.question: What was NVIDIA's GAAP gross margin in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026?
questions.source: Earnings call 2026, CFO remarks (Colette Kress) — 75.0% GAAP, 75.2% non-GAAP

questions.question: How many employees did NVIDIA have at the end of fiscal year 2026, and how were they split between functions?
questions.source: 10-K 2026, p. 8, Item 1 Human Capital Management — ~42,000 employees in 38 countries; 31,000 in R&D, 11,000 in sales, marketing, operations and administration

questions.question: What revenue is NVIDIA guiding to for the first quarter of fiscal year 2027?
questions.source: Earnings call 2026, outlook section — $78 billion, plus or minus 2%

questions.question: How much did NVIDIA invest in Anthropic, and what does the partnership involve?
questions.source: Earnings call 2026, Jensen Huang remarks — $10 billion investment; Anthropic to train and inference on Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems

questions.question: What is the Rubin platform, and which chips make it up?
questions.source: Earnings call 2026, CFO remarks — six chips: Vera CPU, Rubin GPU, NVLink 6 switch, ConnectX-9 SuperNIC, BlueField-4 DPU, Spectrum-6 Ethernet switch

questions.question: What agreement did NVIDIA reach with Groq, and what precedent does the company compare it to?
questions.source: Earnings call 2026, Jensen Huang remarks — non-licensing agreement for low-latency inference technology plus an engineering team; explicitly compared to the Mellanox playbook

questions.question: Is NVIDIA currently generating data center revenue in China, and what does its guidance assume?
questions.source: Earnings call 2026, CFO remarks — small H200 volumes approved by the U.S. government but no revenue generated yet; no China data center compute revenue assumed in the outlook

questions.question: How large was NVIDIA's sovereign AI business in fiscal year 2026, and which countries drove it?
questions.source: Earnings call 2026, CFO remarks — over $30 billion, more than tripled year over year; driven by Canada, France, the Netherlands, Singapore and the UK

questions.question: How does NVIDIA describe its long-term opportunity in physical AI and robotics?
questions.source: Earnings call 2026, CFO remarks — over $6 billion of FY2026 revenue; robotaxi fleets scaling to millions of vehicles, Cosmos and Isaac GR00T models. Automotive context in 10-K 2026, Item 1 (pp. 3-5).

questions.question: Why did NVIDIA acquire Mellanox, and how big has the networking business become since?
questions.source: 10-K 2026, p. 1, Item 1 Business (2020 acquisition, enabled data-center-scale platforms) + earnings call 2026 (over $31 billion in FY2026, more than 10x fiscal 2021)

questions.question: What does NVIDIA say about how data center power constraints shape customer purchasing decisions?
questions.source: Earnings call 2026, CFO remarks — every data center is power constrained, so customers make architectural decisions on performance per watt to maximise AI factory revenue

questions.question: What risks does NVIDIA identify in relation to U.S. export controls and China?
questions.source: 10-K 2026, Item 1A Risk Factors, pp. 23-25 (export licensing, lost China revenue, Chinese competitors); background in Item 1 at pp. 7-8

questions.question: How concentrated is NVIDIA's customer base, and why does the company flag it as a risk?
questions.source: 10-K 2026, p. 38, Concentration of Revenue — one direct customer represented 22% of total revenue and another 14% in FY2026

questions.question: How much was Jensen Huang paid in fiscal year 2026?
questions.source: Not in the corpus. 10-K 2026, p. 44 shows Item 11 Executive Compensation is incorporated by reference to the Proxy Statement, which is not part of this dataset. Sounds like it belongs in a financial filing, so it is a realistic trap — the agent should say the figure is not available rather than invent one.

questions.question: Which company is the direct customer that represented 22% of NVIDIA's revenue in fiscal year 2026?
questions.source: Not in the corpus. 10-K 2026, p. 38 discloses the percentage but deliberately never names the customer. The share is answerable, the identity is not — the agent should say so rather than guess a hyperscaler.

questions.question: What is NVIDIA's market share in AI accelerators compared with AMD and Intel?
questions.source: Not in the corpus. The 10-K describes competition qualitatively in Item 1 and Item 1A but publishes no market-share figures, and no competitor filings are included.

questions.question: What is the strategic rationale behind Mistral AI's acquisition of NVIDIA?
questions.source: Not in the corpus, and the premise is false — no such acquisition happened or could plausibly happen. Unlike the other unanswerable questions, this one tests whether the agent challenges a false premise or accepts it and confabulates a rationale, which is a distinct and common failure mode.
